title: etbb-july-2024-may-2025-update.pdf — section 160
text:
180. Judgments and reasons for decisions always need to be clear, but language and approach
is especially important when vulnerable parties and witnesses are involved:
• Using an easy language paragraph that summarises the decision; this is especially of
benefit to litigants with learning disorders or to children.
117
• For written judgments, there are tools online to make language simpler and which will
assist judges to write for a person with low literacy skills.
118
• The judgment in A Council v Jack's Mother, Jack's Dad and Jack is an example of clarity
in explaining to a parent with a learning disability the reason for the decision.119
• In Lancashire County Council v Mr A, Mr B, The Children, Jackson J explained that the
judgment was as short as possible so that the mother and older children could follow it.120
